# Workflow

Read these rules before you push, or when you change the workspace, a profile, the consumer project, a host cleartext contract, or a host generator. This page holds the full text of the live rules of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

<a id="fr-04"></a>

## FR-04: This package is a workspace member driven from the root `[STALE]`

> This package is a member of the workspace, and every verb runs from the root through a `make` target.

Old number: 1.4.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/foundry.toml:3` and `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/remappings.txt:3-4` show that `forge-std` resolves from the local soldeer `dependencies/`, not from `../../node_modules`. Fix: correct the dependency sentence. Only the npm packages resolve from `../../node_modules`.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-28: Must every npm verb have a `make` target? `test:fork-debug` has none.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-36: Does a rule that repeats one sentence of another rule count as `[CONFLICT]`?

Issues: I-28, I-36.

#### This package is two members of the root workspace

The root `package.json` lists both folders of this package in `workspaces`, and `npm-manifest.json` describes both:

| Folder                        | npm name               | What it is            |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------- |
| `foundry/forge-fhevm-std`     | `@fhevm/forge-std-dev` | The dev package       |
| `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg` | `@fhevm/forge`         | The published package |

A member has no `node_modules` of its own. The workspace installs each dependency once, in the `node_modules` of the root. So `libs` in `foundry.toml` and the lines of `remappings.txt` point at `../../node_modules`, never at a local copy.

#### Run every verb from the root, through `make`

Every verb of this package has a `make` target. Run the target from the root of the repository.

| Target                    | What it runs                                                    |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compile-forge-std`       | The compilation                                                 |
| `lint-forge-std`          | The lint                                                        |
| `test-forge-std`          | The offline tests                                               |
| `test-forge-std-fork`     | The fork tests. This target is opt-in.                          |
| `test-forge-std-fork-url` | The tests under `forge test --fork-url`. This target is opt-in. |
| `test-forge-std-anvil`    | The anvil tests. This target is opt-in.                         |

`compile-forge-std` runs after `compile-cleartext-v-cur`, because the payload of this package is copied from `<vN>`, the current host generation.

#### The root targets include this package

- `make generate` and `make clean-generated` run this package after `<vN>`. `make check-generated` runs both, so it proves the whole chain in the diagram of [FR-20](../entries/FR-20.md).
- `make check-pre` checks the `package.json`, the scripts, the lockfile, and the lint policy of this package against [the npm rules](../../../fhevm-npm/rules/README.md).

#### The consumer test is a Foundry project

The published package has a consumer test in `test-consumer/esm`, as [NR-54](../../../fhevm-npm/rules/entries/NR-54.md) requires. The consumer test is a Foundry project, not a Node script. It uses `@fhevm/forge` as a user does:

- `package.json` installs `@fhevm/forge` by name, with `forge-std`, `@fhevm/solidity`, and `encrypted-types`. `forge-std` is a git dependency, pinned to the tag that this package vendors.
- `remappings.txt` points every prefix into `node_modules`.
- `src/AplusB.sol` is the dApp.
- `test/AplusB.t.sol` inherits `TestFhevm`. It encrypts the inputs, runs the dApp, and decrypts the result.
- `npm test` runs `forge build && forge test`.

The `foundry.toml` of the consumer test does not extend `foundry.base.toml`. It repeats the `[fmt]` policy inline. The consumer test is a standalone project that the test runner copies out of the tree, where no `foundry.base.toml` exists. This is the one exception of [NR-30](../../../fhevm-npm/rules/entries/NR-30.md).

In the copy, `forge lint` and `forge test` work only after `npm install`.

## FR-26: Two different address techniques `[STALE]`

> Templates keep placeholder markers that the deploy patches, and `LocalHostBytecode.sol` is rebuilt with the real addresses.

Old number: 4.1.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/_host/LibForgeFhevmUpgrade.sol:197,265,309` show that `LibHostUpgradeCode.creationCodeFor` also patches for the cleartext swap (`upgradeToCleartext`) and for the cleartext generation upgrade, and the rule permits it for the one-generation upgrade only. Fix: list the three uses. The fix depends on D11.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-36: Does a rule that repeats one sentence of another rule count as `[CONFLICT]`?
- Pending owner decision, issue I-38: Is the bytecode patching meant for all three upgrade paths, or only the one-generation upgrade?

Issues: I-36, I-38, I-122.

- **Templates** (`generate:templates`) keep placeholder markers — addresses derived as
  `keccak256("fhevm.placeholder.<NAME>")[0:20]` — compiled in as literals, and record the byte
  offsets where they land so the TS deploy can overwrite them at deploy time. Hence the ordering: the
  placeholder file is written _before_ `forge build`, or the previous run's markers stay baked in at
  the recorded offsets.
- **`LocalHostBytecode.sol`** (`generate:local-host-bytecode`) deliberately does NOT patch for the
  local deploy. It derives the deployer from the mnemonic, precomputes the nonce sequence's addresses,
  writes them as a real config, rebuilds, and reads the creation bytecode straight out of the artifacts.
  ONE EXCEPTION, and only this one: the upgrade tables it also emits (`*_UPGRADE_CREATION_CODE`,
  `*_UPGRADE_SITES`) exist so [FR-19a](../entries/FR-19a.md) can deploy those same host implementations beside a REMOTE stack,
  whose addresses are not known at generation time and cannot be compiled in. That patching is
  `LibHostUpgradeCode`, it is cheatcode-free and pure, and it is permitted for upgrading an existing
  deployed remote non-cleartext stack one generation behind — for nothing else. In particular the local
  deploy still recompiles, and the generator measures every site's offset in the blob it SHIPS rather
  than reusing the template offsets: solc pools address constants by value, so two builds order them
  differently (`POOL_REORDER_EXEMPT` is that same fact, from the other side).

## FR-27: `patch-sites.json` is a tripwire `[HOLD]`

> `patch-sites.json` is a baseline that a person refreshes after reading the diff, never a build input.

Old number: 4.2.

Check: missing.

Issues: I-14, I-122.

It records how many bytecode sites each
placeholder is patched at, per contract. A count falling to zero means a deploy would bake in a
marker. `generate:patch-sites` is deliberately outside every chain: refreshing the baseline is a
human decision, made after reading the diff.

## FR-28: After touching a cleartext contract `[HOLD]`

> After you change a cleartext contract, regenerate and test the host package, then regenerate this package.

Old number: 4.3.

Check: missing.

Issues: I-01, I-14, I-15, I-36.

A cleartext contract has its source in the host package, `host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>`. This package
holds only a generated copy of it, in `pkg/src/_host/` ([FR-20](../entries/FR-20.md)). A change reaches this package
only when both packages generate again, in this order:

1. In the host package, run `npm run generate`. It rebuilds the files generated from the contracts,
   including the bytecode that the test stack deploys.
2. In the host package, run `forge test`. It tests the change in the package where you made it.
3. In this package, run `npm run generate`. It copies the new payload of the host package into
   `pkg/src/_host/`.

For example, you fix a bug in `CleartextFHEVMExecutor.sol`:

```bash
cd host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>
# You edit pkg/src/cleartext/CleartextFHEVMExecutor.sol.
npm run generate   # 1. Rebuilds the generated files and the bytecode.
forge test         # 2. Tests the fix in the host package.
cd ../../foundry/forge-fhevm-std
npm run generate   # 3. Copies the fix into pkg/src/_host/.
```

If you skip step 3, the tests of this package still run the old copy, without your fix, and pass.

If the contract is `CleartextFHEVMExecutor`, also check
`ContractSizeLimits.t.sol` — it must stay under EIP-170, while the `…Forge` variant is exempt and
deliberately over. `FhevmVm` is exempt too: it is ETCHED (`vm.etch` skips the creation-time check) and may
grow past 24 KB by design; write no size test against it.

#### Before you push

Run these checks, first in the host package, which is the source, then in this package, which consumes it:

```bash
# The host package, the source.
cd host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>
npm run generate && npm run forge:fmt && npm run forge:lint && forge test
MAINNET_RPC_URL=… forge test --match-contract Fork

# This package, the consumer. From the workspace root, the same runs through make:
#   make compile-forge-std lint-forge-std test-forge-std     # or everything: make ci-fast
cd ../../foundry/forge-fhevm-std
npm run generate && npm run lint && forge test
npm run test:consumer                    # the installed @fhevm/forge, by name (FR-04)
SEPOLIA_RPC_URL=… MAINNET_RPC_URL=… npm run test:fork
ARBITRUM_RPC_URL=… MAINNET_RPC_URL=… npm run test:fork        # adds the cleartext-on-a-foreign-chain suite (FR-21)
ARBITRUM_RPC_URL=… MAINNET_RPC_URL=… npm run test:fork-debug  # the same under the fhevm-debug profile (FR-22)
SEPOLIA_RPC_URL=… npm run test:fork-url  # the born-on-a-fork suite, under `forge test --fork-url`
npm run test:anvil                       # starts a throwaway anvil on 8546, runs test/anvil, stops it
```

Use the npm scripts of the host package, not bare `forge fmt` or `forge lint`. The host package keeps the payload under a second profile (`src = pkg/forge/src`), so a bare command formats and lints only `pkg/src`, and reports a clean payload it never looked at. `forge:fmt` and `forge:lint` run all three profiles. The gap does not show in the host package. It shows here, on the generated copy.

If a test says "No tests found in project!" right after you restore or rename a file, the cause is the incremental cache of forge, not the test. Run `forge build --force`, then run the test again.

Both packages end with zero lint notes, zero unused imports, and a clean `forge fmt --check`.

For a stack-too-deep check, loop on `forge build --skip test`, which takes about 0.7 seconds. `forge test` alone does not see a source change that must pass through `generate` to reach the deployed bytecode. The stack is deployed from bytecode generated beforehand, so an edit that is not regenerated tests nothing.
